papers.title: Stability of Plasma Echo Growth and the Sharp Sobolev Stability Threshold for the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau Equation
papers.abstract:
We establish stability of growing plasma echo cascades for the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau equation with Coulomb collisions near a global Maxwellian. The occurrence of plasma echoes, or even a growing cascade in a reduced model, does not by itself establish this stability. We prove that the amplification persists under changes in the linearized operator, including collisions and the exact evolving background coefficients, and under nonlinear perturbations. This yields optimality of the exponent $1/3$ obtained by Chaturvedi, Luk, and Nguyen in the Sobolev stability threshold. Specifically, we construct solutions with initial Sobolev perturbations of size $
u^{1/3}[\log(1/
u)]^p$ whose transport profiles exhibit norm inflation before the enhanced-dissipation time scale $
u^{-1/3}$. Since collisions preclude the backward Sobolev construction used in collisionless echo arguments, we prepare the initial data at physical time zero and control the entire forward evolution.

papers.title: Hugoniot Relation for Multi-Temperature Euler Equations of Compressible Plasma Flows
papers.abstract: Shock solutions for multi-temperature Euler equations are inherently ambiguous due to the loss of microscopic physical detail during model reduction and occurrence of non-conservative terms. This paper presents a detailed analytical study of shock structures in such models. We present two distinct Hugoniot relations, each corresponding to a physically admissible shock solution. Through classical analysis \`a la Courant--Friedrichs, we demonstrate that both satisfy admissibility conditions, revealing a fundamental non-uniqueness in shock structures. By relating these solutions to existing numerical schemes, the structure-preserving and vanishing viscosity approaches, we provide physically justified references for constructing and evaluating discontinuous numerical approximations. In particular, we emphasize that the Hugoniot relation is not uniquely determined by the macroscopic PDEs alone, but must be supplied from external sources such as experiments or first-principles simulations. This insight demonstrates the essential role of microscopic physics in resolving shock ambiguity and contributes to the theoretical foundation for modeling discontinuous plasma flows.

papers.title: Radial Evolution of a Corotating Interaction Region from a High-Resolution MHD Simulation
papers.abstract: Corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are large-scale structures formed by fast--slow solar wind interaction, playing a crucial role in heliospheric dynamics and space weather. However, the evolution of individual CIRs and their full three-dimensional morphology remain poorly understood. We investigate the radial evolution of a single CIR using a high-resolution simulation combined with a backmapping method. The simulation reproduces the major plasma and magnetic signatures observed by Wind at 1~AU and by MAVEN and Tianwen-1 at $\sim$1.6~AU. The CIR exhibits a warped, shell-like spiral structure tilted relative to the heliospheric current sheet, consistent with theoretical predictions. During its developing stage, geometric changes are modest, and the radial scalings of velocity ($V_r \propto r^{0.02}$), density ($N \propto r^{-2.00}$), magnetic field ($B_{\rm total} \propto r^{-1.74}$), and temperature ($T \propto r^{-0.97}$) are comparable to those of the background solar wind. In the mature stage, the CIR drifts in longitude and expands toward high latitudes, while its longitudinal and latitudinal widths decrease with distance. The full-domain scalings change markedly to $V_r \propto r^{0.13}$, $N \propto r^{-1.91}$, $B_{\rm total} \propto r^{0.35}$, and $T \propto r^{-0.52}$, differing from both the background wind and the ecliptic-plane CIR. This study quantifies the radial evolution of a CIR from formation to maturity and highlights the importance of its three-dimensional structure in characterizing its morphology and dynamics.

papers.title: Linear Electrostatic Instabilities Driven by Relativistic Non-Maxwellian Pair Beams
papers.abstract: We investigate how non-Maxwellian momentum distributions affect the linear growth of electrostatic instabilities driven by relativistic pair beams, motivated by the lack of a universally accepted analytical description of blazar-induced pair beams. Different beam distributions are used to describe relativistic pair beams in analytical studies and particle-in-cell simulations. A systematic comparison is therefore needed to determine how the beam distribution influences the instability growth rates. We formulate the relativistic electrostatic response in the weak-beam limit for an anisotropic $\kappa$-type distribution and compare the resulting growth rates with those obtained for Gaussian and Maxwell--J\"uttner distributions. We require $\kappa>3/2$ for a finite root-mean-square momentum spread. For the parameters considered, the $\kappa$-type distributions yield higher maximum growth rates than the Gaussian distribution, even when their mean momenta and momentum spreads are the same. The fastest-growing modes correspond to parallel propagation for the $\kappa$ and Gaussian distributions, whereas the Maxwell--J\"uttner distribution exhibits its maximum for oblique propagation for a mildly relativistic beam. An additional calculation for a highly relativistic pair beam with $\kappa=2$ finds an oblique maximum of the electrostatic growth rate. The beam momentum distribution influences the linear growth of electrostatic instabilities under the conditions investigated.

papers.title: Drift of a Charged Particle in a Black Hole Magnetosphere: the Effect of Black Hole Spin
papers.abstract: Sparse plasma immersed in a strong magnetic field is common in astrophysical scenarios, for which a collisionless description is more appropriate. The guiding-center approximation serves as an effective tool for describing the motion of charged particles in a strong magnetic field, revealing the drift, a sub-leading order motion that causes particles to deviate from the magnetic field lines. It is widely accepted that the charged particles drift under the induction of gravity in Newtonian framework. However, a covariant formulation of the guiding-center approximation, as well as the drift of a charged particle induced by strong gravitational field, has yet to be fully explored. As a preliminary study, we aim to analyze the drift of a single charged particle in a black hole magnetosphere via a covariant approach. Particularly, we focus on the effects of black hole spin. We first examine the drift caused by the rotation of a massive object in the Newtonian regime using the language of gravitoelectromagnetism. A covariant formula of drift is derived, which is confirmed to reduce to the Newtonian results in the weak gravitational field and low speed limit. The impact of BH spin on the drift is analyzed in detail in Kerr spacetime specifically, for which we define the drift rate whose value quantifies the significance of the drift. Our results indicate that the impact of BH spin on the drift of a charged particle in a BH magnetosphere can be comparable to that of other factors in some extreme cases.

papers.title: A generic route to chaos in self-excited plasma oscillations
papers.abstract: We propose a generic autonomous route to chaos in self-excited plasma oscillations through nonlinear feedback from a finite-rate charging variable. Near the threshold of an oscillatory ion-acoustic instability, a multiple-scale reduction yields a Stuart-Landau amplitude equation, represented by a van der Pol-type modal surrogate and coupled to debris-charge evolution in a prototype case of plasma-debris interaction scenario. For a debris-induced ion-ion counter-streaming instability, charge-dependent forcing and frequency modulation, finite charging relaxation, phase-lagged modal response, mixed nonlinear feedback, and saturation form a closed dynamical system without an externally imposed periodic driver. Numerical bifurcation and Lyapunov analyses reveal multistability and a bounded chaotic branch reached through period doubling bifurcation and band formation. We test the proposed mechanism using a one-dimensional open-boundary \emph{hybrid} particle-in-cell-Monte Carlo collision simulation incorporating particle collection, photoemission, secondary-electron emission, and surface regulation. Weak-form sparse regression identifies finite intervals whose projected dynamics reproduce the sign structure of the reduced model, while independent $0$-$1$ chaos test, nonlinear predicatbility, surrogate-data, and Lyapunov diagnostics provide localized evidence of deterministic chaotic organization in the subsonic case. The combined results establish a proof-of-principle route by which a self-excited plasma mode can become chaotic through internally generated charging feedback.

papers.title: Control variates with neural surrogates for uncertainty quantification in kinetic equations
papers.abstract: Efficient uncertainty quantification for kinetic equations with random inputs is challenging because it requires repeated simulations of high-dimensional models, such as the Boltzmann, Landau, and related collisional equations, whose computational cost can quickly become prohibitive. Multifidelity control variates address this difficulty by coupling a small number of high-fidelity simulations with many evaluations of lower-complexity reduced models. In this work, we analyze the case in which the reduced model is replaced by a neural surrogate rather than evaluated through a classical numerical scheme. We show that the resulting estimator remains unbiased and that the change in the optimal variance induced by the neural approximation is controlled by the error between the exact low-fidelity observable and its neural approximation. This estimate is then combined with residual stability estimates for inhomogeneous Fokker--Planck and Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook surrogates. We also extend the analysis to several control variates and to an asymptotic-preserving (AP) hierarchy containing the limiting Euler observable. In the fluid limit, the optimal hierarchical variance converges to the variance associated with the limiting Euler control, while the contribution of the intermediate kinetic correction vanishes. Numerical tests based on micro--macro neural surrogates illustrate the predicted variance stability and the behavior of the AP hierarchy.

papers.title: Simulations of turbulent heat and particle transport in stellarator plasmas
papers.abstract: Achieving sustained energy production in magnetic confinement fusion reactors requires a deep understanding of turbulent transport of heat and particles. This thesis investigates turbulent transport with a particular emphasis on stellarators, using simulations with the $\delta f$ gyrokinetic code stella for the W7-X, LHD, TJ-II and NCSX stellarators, the ASDEX Upgrade (AUG) tokamak and the Cyclone Base Case (CBC). It addresses two questions: how do density gradients affect turbulent heat transport, and can turbulence help retain particles in the plasma core? In the first part, an inter-machine study shows a strong reduction of the ion heat flux in NCSX and W7-X with increasing density gradients, attributed to the stabilization of ion-temperature-gradient-driven modes without significantly destabilizing trapped-electron modes or universal instabilities. This beneficial effect is absent in tokamaks, where the heat flux increases with the density gradient, highlighting the role of magnetic geometry. The ion heat flux in stellarators does not follow the growth rate of the fastest-growing linear mode, underscoring the importance of nonlinear effects. Trapped-electron modes dominate in CBC, AUG, TJ-II, LHD and NCSX, while passing-particle-driven universal instabilities contribute significantly in W7-X. The second part addresses the long-standing discrepancy between the strongly hollow density profiles predicted by neoclassical theory in large stellarators and the flat or weakly peaked profiles measured in W7-X. Nonlinear simulations and a particle balance analysis show that turbulence provides a robust inward particle flux, driven by finite ion and electron temperature gradients, that can account for the observed profiles: the sign of the turbulent particle flux matches the sign of the discrepancy between the experimental and neoclassical fluxes across the entire plasma radius of W7-X.

papers.title: Gas expansion in global models of nanosecond pulsed discharges: a reduced gas-dynamic model coupled to plasma kinetics
papers.abstract: Global (zero-dimensional) kinetic models of nanosecond pulsed discharges describe the expansion of the heated gas channel (kernel) with simplified gas-dynamic closures. We show that these closures can lead to errors of tens of percent in the calculated gas density, temperature and species densities, especially in the first microseconds after every pulse. Here, we propose a fast, reduced gas-dynamic model of Lagrangian shells, closed by an approximate cylindrical acoustic radiation condition, with no fitted physical coefficient. The reduced model reproduces the axis density obtained by verified one- dimensional compressible computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations within 2.4% for smooth deposition profiles and axis pressures up to six times ambient, typically a thousand times faster than CFD. We couple it with our in-house global plasma-kinetics solver (SoPlasma-0D), whose energy partition after the pulse agrees well with that derived from measurements and with an independent calculation. Two microseconds after a single pulse in air, and compared with the proposed coupled model, the existing closures overestimate the axis density by up to a factor of 2.8, the atomic oxygen density by up to 2.7 and the temperature by up to 680 K. For repetitive pulses 200 or 430 ns apart, of equal energy per unit volume, no existing closure follows the coupled model at both intervals, in the gas density met by each later pulse and in the energy per molecule deposited by late pulses, which sets how strongly they dissociate and heat the gas. The proposed reduced model should therefore be used to describe the gas evolution during the expansion phase after every nanosecond pulse, and for repetitive pulses above about 100 kHz in kernels of radius up to about a millimetre.

papers.title: Analytic Model for Transient Plateau Filling in Vibrational Distributions of Periodically Driven Plasmas
papers.abstract: In periodically driven molecular plasmas, the vibrational distribution function is governed by the competition between vibration--vibration (V-V) up-pumping along the anharmonic ladder and vibration--translation (V-T) relaxation, producing the Treanor--Gordiets distribution. When vibrational energy accumulates across cycles faster than V-V exchange can populate the upper levels, the Gordiets plateau remains transiently depleted. Existing algebraic models assume a quasi-steady plateau, whereas exact transient solutions of the nonlinear V-V diffusion equation require the elapsed time since excitation and the source strength, which are unavailable in multidimensional simulations that track only local macroscopic variables. Here, elapsed time is replaced by a local vibrational energy timescale formed from the vibrational energy per molecule and its period-averaged rate of change. This reduces the diffusion equation in level space to an ordinary differential equation solved in closed form without linearization, yielding a level-dependent correction to the steady plateau governed by a single dimensionless group: the number of V-V collisions per energy timescale weighted by the plateau amplitude at the Treanor minimum. The distribution front advances as the square root of this group, and the steady distribution is recovered as the group grows large. Compared with state-to-state master-equation calculations for N$_2$ under nanosecond pulse trains spanning 300-1500 K, 0.041-1 atm, and 1-100 kHz (1440 sampled states), the model reduces the 90th-percentile error in level populations from 1.88 decades for the steady model and 1.32 decades for an adapted self-similar solution to 0.53 decades, at essentially the evaluation cost of the steady model.

papers.title: A spherical body in plasma simulated with adaptive mesh and algorithm refinement
papers.abstract: An absorbing sphere in a weakly ionized plasma is the oldest kinetic problem of probe theory. It presents key difficulties in plasma simulation: disparate velocity scales, orbital motion, phase-space regions that no characteristic of the plasma reaches, a boundary set by a kinetic flux balance, and collisions that qualitatively change the answer. We use this problem to demonstrate the Plasma Adaptive Mesh and Algorithm Refinement (PAMAR) framework introduced in a companion paper. Electrons and ions have separate solvers on their own adaptive $(r,v,\mu)$ octrees, or on reduced phase spaces at the angular-moment level (Fokker-Planck and two-stream models), coupled through a radial Poisson field solver. Two exact references, a method of characteristics for the collisionless problem and integration along the orbits for elastic scattering, audit the solvers. We compute the current-voltage characteristic of the probe on both electron and ion branches, and the profiles of the potential and of the moments of both species agree with the exact solution. Far from the sphere, the potential follows the Coulomb law in neither limit: it falls as $r^{-2}$ without collisions and as $r^{-1}$ only beyond the ion mean free path. With elastic electron scattering, the kinetic solver follows the exact dependence of the collected current on the mean free path, from free flight toward diffusion, to 1 percent. Finally, we demonstrate the ion model selection cell by cell, using a fluid model coupled to the kinetic solver, with the interface set by the pressure anisotropy; with charge exchange, a sensor of ion trapping is also needed. According to exact solutions, the ion anisotropy extends to several probe radii, much farther than the electron loss cone.

papers.title: Scaling of the Radial Motion and Size of Filamentary Structures in the Scrape-Off Layer Inferred from 100 kHz Visible Imaging on 294 MAST Discharges
papers.abstract: Filaments are important carriers of cross-field transport in the scrape-off layer of a tokamak. Analytic models predict that their radial velocity varies with their size. We measured the radial velocity and size of a large population of filaments on MAST, using data recorded from a 100 kHz, 48 x 256 pixel camera in the outboard midplane in the FAIR-MAST archive. Computer vision techniques were used to automate the identification of filaments and tracking of their trajectories, which yielded 86,042 filament tracks over 294 discharges in 4 campaigns. The archive does not contain spatial calibration, so we have obtained a pixel scale by regression of the plasma limb column in the image on the EFIT outboard LCFS radius, with bootstrap intervals. The scale is 2.7-5.2 millimetres per pixel. We find a median velocity of 424 m/s, and median radial width of 3.6 cm. The dependence of velocity on size is mild, with a log-log slope of +0.05 (95% interval +0.03 to +0.07) when the effects of exposure blurring are corrected for. This is because filaments are not in either velocity regime; they span the range $\hat{a}$ = 0.13-1.97 in two-region units, which straddles the maximum velocity predicted by the two-region model, but the normalized velocity $\hat{v}$ is much smaller than the scale of the model, at $\hat{v} \approx 0.06$.

papers.title: A full-wave ICRH solver with full kinetic accuracy using only first order differential equations
papers.abstract: Accurate full-wave computation of ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) typically requires solving the computationally demanding integro-differential dielectric tensor of the hot plasma. Based on the method in [Phys. Plasmas 32, 082110 (2025)], we develop BO-FW1D, a 1D frequency domain finite difference full-wave solver which generates full kinetic, accurate and efficient simulations utilizing a fluid plasma model. To accurately convert the conductivity tensor in phase space into a first-order differential equation, we introduce a mathematically rigorous framework using pseudodifferential operator theory based on Kohn-Nirenberg ordering. Benchmarks with an all-orders 1D full-wave solver show high consistency in critical kinetic effects and electric-field distributions, while substantial computational acceleration is achieved. This work could lay the foundation for developing full-wave solvers that combine full kinetic accuracy with high computational efficiency.

papers.title: Cold stellarator coils that outlast power plant lifetime
papers.abstract: We show that a two order-of-magnitude reduction in stellarator coil peak neutron flux and heating can be achieved by moving coils much farther from the plasma if the plasma shape may change slightly and the vessel shielding is increased. Alternating coil and plasma optimizations move the closest coils of our main design over 25 cm out, without substantial degradation in key engineering and physics requirements. The field error decreases and the plasma boundary moves about 1 cm on average. Such coils would be at 4.2 K, use only one third to half the superconducting tape of the original, and require no replacement during the plant's lifetime. This reduced coil flux and heating could significantly enhance the viability of stellarator power plants.

papers.title: Embedded Trigger Control System for Wave--Plasma Interaction Experiments in Large Volume Plasma Device
papers.abstract: {Magnetic-field control and synchronization are essential requirements in laboratory plasma experiments investigating wave propagation and plasma instabilities. In this work, an Embedded Trigger Control System (ETCS) has been designed and implemented for synchronized operation of a pulsed Helmholtz coil system and a broadband whistler-wave exciter in the Large Volume Plasma Device--Upgrade (LVPD-U). The experimental configuration employs an electrostatically shielded loop antenna driven by a thyratron-switched pulse-forming network to launch broadband whistler waves in the frequency range of approximately 150~kHz to 5~MHz. Simultaneously, a pulsed Helmholtz coil capable of generating magnetic fields up to $\pm150$~G is used to modify the local magnetic topology and create transient magnetic-null configurations. The developed ETCS utilizes the controlled evolution of the Helmholtz circuit $L/R$ time constant through the introduction of a lumped series inductor, enabling precise magnetic-field ramping and dynamic timing control. A microcontroller-based trigger architecture determines the desired firing instant from the calibrated current evolution of the Helmholtz circuit and synchronizes wave excitation with a prescribed magnetic-field amplitude. The system extends the effective circuit time constant by more than an order of magnitude, allowing accurate and repeatable wave launching during controlled magnetic-field evolution. The implemented approach provides a simple, reliable, and versatile synchronization platform for wave--plasma interaction studies requiring precise temporal coordination between pulsed magnetic-field generation and wave excitation.

papers.title: Experimental observation of higher-harmonic generation of whistler waves in magnetized plasma of Large Volume Plasma Device
papers.abstract: We report the higher-harmonic generation of whistler waves using a loop antenna in the Large Volume Plasma Device (LVPD). The antenna is energized using a pulse-forming network (PFN), and the excited magnetic fluctuations are measured using a three-axis B-dot probe. Experiments are performed in a moderate-density ($n_e \sim 1-2 \times 10^{17}\ \text{m}^{-3}$), low-temperature ($T_e \sim 2-5\ \text{eV}$) argon plasma in a uniform axial magnetic field ($B_z \sim 6.2\ \text{G}$). A Helmholtz coil is employed to investigate the dependence of the wave response and propagation on the local magnetic-field configuration. A clear distinction between wave characteristics is observed in the absence and presence of plasma: in plasma, the excited wave shows a significant $\delta B_y$ component along with $\delta B_x$, indicating polarization. In addition to the fundamental frequency, distinct spectral peaks are observed at $300\ \text{kHz}$, $450\ \text{kHz}$, and $600\ \text{kHz}$. These harmonics indicate nonlinear wave-plasma interactions, and bicoherence analysis further provides evidence of nonlinear coupling between the observed frequency components. The spatial propagation of the wave was systematically diagnosed using a linear array of five identical B-dot probes. Spatial cross-correlation analysis reveals strong structural coherence during wave propagation, allowing the explicit experimental determination of the wave phase velocity ($V_{ph}$) and parallel wave number ($k_{\parallel}$) for the generated higher harmonics. The measured propagation is oblique at an angle of approximately $48^\circ$ with respect to the background magnetic field, and the experimental dispersion relation agrees with the cold-plasma oblique whistler dispersion relation within experimental uncertainty.

papers.title: Deriving the Continuous $\beta$-FPUT Model for Decayless Solar Coronal Oscillations Directly from Resistive MHD
papers.abstract: We present an analytical framework deriving the fluid-continuum $\beta$-Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou ($\beta$-FPUT) system directly from a third-order resistive magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) expansion to explain persistent, decayless transverse oscillations observed in solar coronal loops. For a continuous wave field propagating along a longitudinal magnetic field with cross-field density variations, a multi-scale expansion demonstrates that quadratic $\mathcal{O}(2)$ advective and Maxwell tension terms vanish identically due to out-of-plane polarization symmetry. Instead, the quadratic longitudinal ponderomotive force drives field-aligned density modulations that back-react on the primary transverse wave, yielding a cubic $\mathcal{O}(3)$ restoring force. In the long-wavelength limit, the governing equations reduce to a fluid-continuum Modified Korteweg-de Vries (mKdV) system where cross-field profile variation provides the non-linear dispersive mechanism. We prove that this internal fluid mechanism establishes stable, amplitude-dependent frequency self-focusing, which phase-locks adjacent elements and prevents phase-mixing wave attenuation without requiring external steady driving parameterizations. This framework enables macro-scale coronal seismology, providing closed-form expressions to invert observed decayless wave-packet durations to compute the unresolved cross-field density gradient scale length ($L_x$) and the internal volumetric filling factor ($f_V$) without relying on traditional emission measure or spectroscopic line-ratio diagnostics. Much like famous Enrico Fermi's historic use of macro-scale displacements to estimate complex atomic explosion yields, this framework establishes a paradigm where monitoring macroscopic oscillation durations empowers observers to extract fine-scale, otherwise unresolvable waveguide properties.

papers.title: LADA: A differential algebra-based simulation package for arbitrary-order charged-particle and light optics
papers.abstract: LADA computes charged-particle and light-optical transfer maps by differential algebra in Python, with run-time order selection validated through order nine. It combines these established map methods with ATIMA-based stopping, straggling and scattering, the GLOBAL, CHARGE and ETACHA charge-state models, EPAX fragmentation, six-dimensional integration through measured or computed RF fields with reference-energy rebasing, and section-wise particle tracking with aperture and RF-window losses. Maps retain analytic dependence on external parameters; contraction with input moments gives beam observables and their sensitivities without particle tracking at each setting. Lattice import from COSY, MAD-X, Xsuite and MIRKO provides per-record status and comparisons with available codes. NumPy is the only required dependency. On the HHT benchmark, where the maps of both codes agree in every coefficient through ninth order, the optional compiled DA kernel on eight cores is 1.5 to 1.6 times faster than COSY at orders 3 to 9. Applications include the SIBAF irradiation facility through CALINA, proton microscopy and beam-line studies at GSI and FAIR.

papers.title: Shape effects on the Shafranov shift of Solov'ev equilibria with prescribed boundaries
papers.abstract: The Shafranov shift, the outward displacement of the magnetic axis of a toroidal plasma, is known analytically for circular and elliptical cross-sections, whereas its dependence on shape in strongly shaped plasmas has not been studied systematically. Here the shift is analyzed for a wide range of prescribed boundaries, at fixed profiles or poloidal beta, using exact Solov'ev solutions of the Grad--Shafranov equation with the boundary imposed in a least-squares sense. For shaped boundaries the shift depends on the point from which it is measured, usually the geometric center, the midpoint of the radial extent of the boundary. Therefore, a straight-cylinder equilibrium with the same plasma shape is introduced as the zero-shift reference state, and the shift is measured from its magnetic axis. With this reference, some known features of the shift measured from the geometric center turn out to be effects of the reference point, whose error depends only on the boundary and can also make the shift negative. Three boundary parametrizations are used to analyze positive and negative triangularity, squareness from square to concave shapes, and non-convex star polygons of arbitrary symmetry order. At fixed poloidal beta the shift depends only weakly on triangularity: the larger shift of negative than of positive triangularity plasmas obtained with the geometric center is an effect of the reference point and nearly disappears with the cylindrical reference. Negative squareness and concavity, instead, reduce the shift itself: for concave plasma cross-sections it is almost half that of elliptical and D-shaped ones.

papers.title: Data-driven non-contiguous photon-energy groups for fast multigroup radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas
papers.abstract: Radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas, such as extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light source plasma, laser-fusion hohlraums, and stellar interiors, needs too many photon-energy groups for accurate radiation-hydrodynamic simulations. Our data-driven method assigns the bins of an opacity table to $K$ non-contiguous groups with fixed spectral shapes that never couple. Existing multigroup codes can use it by replacing the opacity table.In a radiation-hydrodynamic code, 30 such groups replaced 151 conventional groups; the energy conversion efficiency from laser to EUV changed by less than 0.5\% in absolute value.
